clue.text: Wrongly locating organ around end of nave for churchgoers

indicators.note: the jumbled words sit around the single letter taken from nave
done wrongly, the letters of the two words are put in a different order
the end of nave is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone has misplaced the church organ, putting it beyond the end of the nave where worshippers sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' looks like a comment on the misplaced organ but is the anagram signal; 'around' and 'end of' finish the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective relating to a congregation, the body of worshippers attending a church service.

clue.text: Nudist heading off after vehicle, I see — one makes an amusing picture

indicators.note: the trimmed nudist comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
C sounds like 'see', the usual crossword shorthand

indicators.note: the nudist loses the first letter, the head of the word

parts.note: a naturist is a nudist

explanation.surface: A nudist drives off in a car, prompting someone to sketch the comic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the N from NATURIST, leaving ATURIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoonist who draws exaggerated, comic portraits is exactly one who makes an amusing picture.

clue.text: One trapped in hub heads for the exit (an inexperienced thought)

indicators.note: the numeral one is held captive inside the word for hub

parts.note: the nave is the hub of a wheel
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at a hub rushes for the way out, which turns out to be a naive idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety means a lack of worldly experience, here shown in an innocent, unworldly notion.

clue.text: Scientist working with server's limitation

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scientist collaborates with a server, whose limitation becomes the issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'server's' is read as 'is', a link joining wordplay to the definition, so only SERVER joins SCIENTIST under the anagram signal 'working'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restrictive is a constraining quality, so the noun means a limit or confinement.

clue.text: American oldie arranged by criminal stealing number

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted out of order
the letter is taken away from the phrase, as if stolen

explanation.surface: An elderly American is set up by a crook who makes off with a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stealing' takes N out of ARRANGED BY, and 'criminal' rearranges the remaining ARRAGEDBY. GRAY is the American spelling of grey.
explanation.definitionFit: An old man, pictured with a grey beard, given in its US spelling to match 'American'.

clue.text: Water in dry getting response from bird

indicators.note: the word for water sits inside the letters meaning dry

parts.note: TT means teetotal, someone who stays dry
wee is informal for urine, making water

explanation.surface: Pouring water into something dry gets a chirp from a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means teetotal (TT), not lacking moisture, and 'Water' is the childish WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short chirping call is the sound a small songbird makes in reply.

clue.text: Monetarist I've so upset — poor risk assessments?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An economist believing in controlling money supply complains that someone has upset them.
explanation.definitionFit: Overestimations are judgements that put a figure too high, hence badly judged risks, with the question mark admitting it is an example.

clue.text: Attorney to yearn to become diplomat?

parts.note: Att. is the abbreviation for attorney
to ache for something is to yearn for it

explanation.surface: A lawyer dreams of joining the diplomatic service.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior member of an embassy staff, so one kind of diplomat, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Politicians, not one special, having time in control, restored jobs

indicators.note: the politicians, with their time added, sit inside the control word

parts.note: reins are what one uses to control a horse

indicators.note: the reduced politicians have the time letter added after them
one of the letters for special is dropped

parts.note: statesmen are senior politicians

explanation.surface: Politicians who regain control after time out restore people to their posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one special' drops just one of the two S letters, and 'having' adds the time letter at the end, making STATEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinstatement is restoring someone to a former position, so in the plural, people put back into their jobs.

clue.text: A positive conclusion in X-ray, say — it is an intestinal problem

indicators.note: the conclusion goes inside the picture word

parts.note: an X-ray is an example of a picture, PIC for short
an end is a conclusion
taken as written, the two words run together

explanation.surface: A positive result on an X-ray reveals a gut complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the appendix, a small pouch off the large bowel, so a disorder of the gut.

clue.text: Cold tragic figure for certain

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
King Lear is the hero of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A tragic character is decidedly chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is clear it is plain and beyond doubt, as in 'it is clear that'.

clue.text: The flower of the dairy tournament?

parts.note: butter is a dairy product
a cup is a knockout tournament, like the FA Cup

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: which bloom is the prize of a dairy competition?
explanation.definitionFit: A common yellow meadow plant with glossy cup-shaped petals.

clue.text: Biting insect pest in WWI?

indicators.note: the pest is found in the trench, so the trench word is named first in the phrase

parts.note: the First World War was fought from trenches
an ant is an insect that can be a pest

explanation.surface: A soldier's question about a nipping bug infesting the World War One front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biting' looks like part of the insect picture, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are incisive and cutting, so biting in the sense of sharply critical.

clue.text: Snap large creature, not insect, in toto

indicators.note: the reduced creature sits inside the letters of toto

parts.note: toto, as in 'in toto', taken as written

indicators.note: the insect is removed from the creature

parts.note: an elephant is a very large animal
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A photographer snaps a whole large animal, but without any insects in shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not insect' leaves ELEPH; 'in toto' is read literally, the reduced creature going inside the word toto.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph taken with a long-focus lens, so a kind of snapshot.

clue.text: Academic documents, mostly items immediately referenced?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: theses are dissertations written for a degree

explanation.surface: Academic papers are mostly about things just mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrative pronoun pointing at things close at hand or just named, the plural of 'this'.

clue.text: Priest curtailed gossip

indicators.note: curtailed means having the tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: to rabbit is to chatter on, informal British usage

explanation.surface: A clergyman cuts short some idle chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher and leader, loosely counted as a priest in crosswords.

clue.text: Some lingerie business needing injection of very great swagger

indicators.note: the letter for very is injected between the lingerie and the business

parts.note: a bra is a piece of lingerie
ado means fuss, business

explanation.surface: A lingerie firm needs a cash injection to keep its confident strut.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a bold, boastful show of confidence, a showy swagger.

clue.text: Determined theologian set about murder, disposing of North American

indicators.note: the theologian is placed around the other letters

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

indicators.note: the letters for North American are got rid of

parts.note: to eliminate someone is to murder them

explanation.surface: A resolute theologian set about a killing, dispatching an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' leaves ELIMITE; DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the usual crossword theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: To delimit is to fix the limits of, so a delimited thing has been fixed or settled.

clue.text: Silent twisting absorbing energy of stretching

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the energy letter
twisting the word round puts its letters in a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Something silent twists around, soaking up energy as it stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensile describes tension, being drawn out or extended, so relating to pulling.

clue.text: Fast transport? You'll get speed on board with it

indicators.note: on here means aboard, so the speed word goes inside the vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the craft one goes on board
pace is speed
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A promise that boarding with this will get you moving quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' conventionally means inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle for travelling through outer space, where it goes very fast, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Complaint with women being overlooked for crucial position

indicators.note: the women letter is ignored, so it drops out

parts.note: a whinge is a moan, British informal

explanation.surface: A complaint that women are passed over for a key post.
explanation.walkthrough: WHINGE is British informal for a moaning complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the pivotal point on which matters depend, a crucial juncture.

clue.text: A lot of fold's turned in internally in garment

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the shortened fold
a lot of means most, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a tuck is a fold sewn into fabric

indicators.note: turned means read backwards

explanation.surface: A dressmaker turns in much of a fold inside a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' leaves TUC, and the 's of fold's is read as 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose, simple tunic is a long shirt-like piece of clothing.

clue.text: With large, long time to record, I will probe history (in US, at least)

definitions.text: With large, long time to record, I will probe history (in US, at least)

indicators.note: the string of pieces goes into the word for history, probing it

parts.note: the past is history
an eon is a vast period of time
to log is to record

explanation.surface: A fossil hunter describes the job: long ages to record while delving into the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the scientist and builds the word. '(in US, at least)' flags the American spelling without an extra A.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil scientist literally probes deep history and records vast stretches of time.

clue.text: Excitement seen in deployment of true obsessions

indicators.note: deploying the letters sets them out in a new order

explanation.surface: Excitement shows when real passions are given free rein.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterousness is rowdy, noisy high spirits, a state of agitated liveliness.
